criteria.title: CQRS Migration with MediatR and Thin Controllers
criteria.description: MediatR is pinned to [12.5.0] with brackets in the csproj (not v13 or v14). All Sprint 1 use cases (IDN-01 to IDN-12 and CAT-01 to CAT-04) along with Campaign endpoints are written as a Command or Query of type IRequest<Result<T>>, each with an independent IRequestHandler in its own slice under Application/Features/<Feature>/<UseCase>/ (request, Handler, Validator, and DTOs). Controllers dispatch solely via ISender/IMediator, contain no business logic or validation code, and map Result to Ok, Created with a Location header, NoContent, or ProblemDetails. Commands write through the Generic Repository and Unit of Work, while Queries read from DbContext with AsNoTracking and project to DTOs using Select. No domain entities are returned from the API. All CORE requirements work via Scalar or Postman.

criteria.title: Result Pattern and Error Catalogue
criteria.description: There is an Error with fields Code, Message, and Type where Type is of an enum named ErrorType, and there are Result and Result<T> with Success and Failure methods. All 20 codes in the SRS §6.1 catalogue are defined as static errors (from Validation.Failed, Auth.*, Category.*, and Campaign.* through Donation.*, Common.RateLimited, File.*, Payment.InvalidSignature, and Idempotency.KeyReusedWithDifferentRequest) with the correct HTTP status codes. The ErrorType-to-HTTP mapping is implemented: Validation 400, Unauthorized 401, Forbidden 403, NotFound 404, Conflict 409, PayloadTooLarge 413, UnprocessableEntity 422, TooManyRequests 429, Failure 500. No exception is thrown for an expected failure (neither AppException nor DomainException in normal flow), and errors are returned as values from the Domain and Handlers.

criteria.title: Automatic Validation via ValidationBehavior
criteria.description: ValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse> implements IPipelineBehavior, is registered in MediatR (e.g., via AddOpenBehavior), and executes all registered IValidator<TRequest> instances before the Handler. On failure, it short-circuits execution immediately and returns Result.Failure with code Validation.Failed and a dictionary of field-level errors, without invoking the Handler. A Validator exists for every Command and Query that has inputs (SRS §6.2), including the registration password policy (8+ chars, uppercase, lowercase, digit) and CreateCampaignCommandValidator. Handlers do not repeat basic input validation, and business rules remain in the Domain. Validation failure returns HTTP 400 with code: Validation.Failed and the errors field.

criteria.title: Unified Error Handling: IExceptionHandler and RFC 9457 ProblemDetails
criteria.description: AddProblemDetails is enabled, and IExceptionHandler catches unexpected exceptions, logs them in full, and returns 500 with a generic ProblemDetails without exception.Message, stack trace, or any internal details. All error responses (expected Result failures, exceptions, and framework errors such as 401 and 403) use the application/problem+json format and include code and traceId, with the errors field for validation errors only. The HTTP status code comes from the ErrorType mapping. Verified with an invalid-data request (400), a non-existent ID (404 Campaign.NotFound), and a rule violation (422 Campaign.GoalBelowRaised).

criteria.title: CancellationToken Propagation and TimeProvider Abstraction
criteria.description: Every Controller action accepts a CancellationToken and passes it to Send, then down to Handlers, Repositories, and asynchronous EF Core methods (ToListAsync, FirstOrDefaultAsync, SaveChangesAsync) without using CancellationToken.None in between. TimeProvider is registered in DI and injected into Handlers, and there is no DateTime.UtcNow or DateTime.Now in the Domain or Handlers; the current time is read via GetUtcNow and passed to entities as a parameter. Date calculations (daysLeft and campaign expiry) rely on TimeProvider.

criteria.title: Optimistic Concurrency Control (CMP-10)
criteria.description: Campaign includes byte[] RowVersion configured with IsRowVersion() via Fluent API. The campaign response returns RowVersion, the client sends it in PUT /campaigns/{id}, and the Handler sets it as the OriginalValue for comparison. DbUpdateConcurrencyException is caught and converted to Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict. Verified by sending two PUT requests with the same rowVersion: the first succeeds and the second returns HTTP 409 with ProblemDetails containing code: Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict.

criteria.title: Campaigns Module (CMP-01 to CMP-06 and CMP-11)
criteria.description: POST /campaigns (Admin only) creates a bilingual campaign with status Active and RaisedAmount = 0 and returns 201 with Location; non-existent category returns 404 Category.NotFound, GoalAmount <= 0 returns 400 Validation.Failed, and a past date returns 422 Campaign.EndDateInPast. PUT /campaigns/{id} (Admin only) enforces invariants 2, 7, and 8 (Campaign.EndDateInPast and Campaign.GoalBelowRaised 422, and Campaign.NotActive 409). DELETE /campaigns/{id} (Admin only) performs a soft delete returning 204, and the deleted campaign never appears in any query. GET /campaigns lists active campaigns and GET /campaigns/success-stories lists completed ones, both without login. GET /campaigns/{id} returns all fields with progressPercent capped at 100 and non-negative daysLeft, and 404 Campaign.NotFound for an unknown ID. Public endpoints return title and description based on Accept-Language (ar returns Arabic; any other value or absence falls back to English), while Admin endpoints return both languages. Rules reside inside entity methods (Campaign.Create and Campaign.Update) rather than in Handlers, and Enums are returned as strings in JSON.

criteria.title: Unit Testing
criteria.description: A test project (DonationHub.UnitTests or two separate projects) with at least 15 passing tests following the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern; dotnet test passes and the solution builds without errors. Moq is pinned to [4.18.4] and FluentAssertions to [7.0.0] (or alternatives NSubstitute and Shouldly). Tests cover domain invariants (goal > 0, past date with a faked TimeProvider, GoalBelowRaised, final state, transition to Completed), calculations (progressPercent and daysLeft), Validators, Handlers with mocked repositories (Category.NotFound without calling SaveChangesAsync, saving once on success, Campaign.NotFound, and mapping DbUpdateConcurrencyException to Campaign.ConcurrencyConflict), pipeline short-circuiting in ValidationBehavior, and unified Auth.InvalidCredentials error. New behavior is covered, with no tests for getters or EF Core itself, and no reliance on the real system clock.

criteria.title: README and Submission
criteria.description: README is updated with: what was added in Sprint 2, how to try it (including Accept-Language and testing a concurrency conflict), and design decisions—most notably the read/write split (Repository/UoW for writes, DbContext with AsNoTracking for reads). The sprint-2 tag exists and points to the latest commit, and any fix is tagged as sprint-2-fix without moving the original tag. No secrets exist in the repository or Git history (keys and passwords are in user-secrets or environment variables only).

criteria.title: Explaining Decisions and Trade-offs
criteria.description: The learner's ability during review to explain the rationale, alternatives, and trade-offs behind their decisions, such as: why reads bypass the Repository while writes go through it, the difference between Command and Query, why Result is used instead of exceptions and when an exception remains appropriate, how MediatR Pipeline Behaviors work along with their execution order and how ValidationBehavior short-circuits execution, how optimistic concurrency with RowVersion works and when pessimistic locking is preferred, why MediatR was pinned to 12.5.0 and FluentAssertions to 7.0.0, what happens to an in-flight query upon request cancellation with and without CancellationToken propagation, and why TimeProvider makes tests deterministic. Answers are evaluated based on understanding rather than memorization.
